application.name: OpticBench posterior-pole eye parameter experiment app

hypothesis: PPT-declared focal-length, axial-length and pupil ranges can be explored as independent manual inputs while preserving the corrected model contract that object demand sets source distance and never drives automatic focal-length fitting.
limitations: The chick axial-length range is explicitly reported by the PPT; the child and adult plus/minus 0.5 mm axial ranges are existing sensitivity assumptions because the PPT supplies only approximate central values.

Corneal and crystalline-lens component ranges are shown as provenance references but are not varied independently because the PPT lacks the spacing, indices, complete radii and principal-plane data required for an identifiable anatomical model.
Non-zero external-lens cases use provisional vertex distances and are rejected when the source distance would place the source on the wrong side of the lens.
Range exploration is paraxial geometric analysis and does not establish absolute irradiance or biological safety.
objective: Extend the dedicated experiment application with a transparent PPT-range exploration mode without weakening the validated three-fixed-focal baseline.
observations: The original 252-case fixed-focal baseline remains unchanged and passes the existing result validator.
A chick case at 7.83 mm focal length, 12.2 mm axial length, 2.7 mm pupil and 85 D demand gives a conservative source diameter of 5.9866957071 mm.
The chick axial-length sensitivity view produces 21 valid points across three axial levels and seven demand levels.
The chick three-level range grid contains 126 valid combinations because the pupil default equals its maximum and duplicate levels are removed.
Desktop and 390 px mobile browser layouts, range sliders, sensitivity selection, range-grid generation, JSON export and CSV export were exercised without browser console errors.
